handback.title: Problems filed publicly show none of the private code
handback.summary: Before the job-hunt trial, problems Dokima files in its public repo stop showing the private repo's code.
handback.user_story: When the trial files a Dokima problem publicly, the owner sees none of job-hunt's files or code there.

acceptance_criteria.text: When a filed problem names a file the private repo holds, Dokima's public repo shows no such path.
acceptance_criteria.words: job-hunt stays private: nothing from it (resumes, profile, leads, companies, people, its code) appears in Dokima's public repo

edge_cases.case: Evidence also names a Dokima file the private repo does not hold: that path still shows.

acceptance_criteria.text: When a filed problem quotes a line of the private repo's code, Dokima's public repo shows no such line.
acceptance_criteria.words: a filed problem names only what Dokima did wrong

edge_cases.case: The same problem's own words around the quoted line still show.

raises.label: Doubt: little code
raises.text: Most of the trial is running it on job-hunt. Should this plan carry only the privacy fix? Plan assumes so.
raises.evidence: Code already covers it: `plan.py` approvers without CODEOWNERS, `tests.exclude` setting, `upstream.py` filing.

raises.label: Trial results untestable here
raises.text: Merges, zero manual fixes, two setup steps and approvals only show on the live trial. Sign off by hand?
raises.evidence: These happen on the private job-hunt repo; no test here can watch them.

raises.label: Names need agent rule
raises.text: Code cannot spot companies, people or resume text in a filed problem. Is the agents' rule enough there?
raises.evidence: `upstream.py` scrub removes only the repo name, links and issue numbers; agents are told the rest.
